frequency_question: How often do central debt managers scale up secondary-market intervention programs past significant operational thresholds once initiated?
membership_rule: Includes formal, announced Treasury or central bank liquidity-support, buyback, or twist programs targeting sovereign debt secondary markets with explicit volume goals. Excludes emergency central bank lender-of-last-resort bank bailouts and routine monetary policy open market operations.

cases.name: US Treasury Buyback and Debt Realignment Exercise
UK Debt Management Office Debt Purchase Operations
US Federal Reserve QE/Treasury Direct Operation Programs (Operation Twist style)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; representative of major developed market sovereign debt liquidity intervention scaling phases.
known_gaps: Excludes minor emerging market debt management interventions due to different structural depth and reserve currency status.
skeleton: Three major sovereign debt management restructuring and liquidity intervention cycles over the past 30 years, each scaling up past initial operational thresholds to achieve structural portfolio goals.
multiplier: 3 cases observed, 3 scaled past initial operational thresholds
validity_reason: Sovereign debt management frameworks evolve slowly over multi-decade structural regimes.
